findings.where: Nav bar, the home logo top left (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The logo appears all in white. Its blue wordmark (#0070C0) and grey arches (#404040) are gone. The brand sheet holds only the full-colour logo, and no white version has been approved. Recolouring the logo to suit the blue ground is the one thing the house rules forbid; the fix is to change the ground or use a version Mark has approved.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo is the one fixed part of his identity and must stay as it is. Shown this tile, he sees his mark in colours he never approved and can't judge whether the blueprint look works with his real logo.

findings.fault: The six-colour palette leaves out the logo's blue and grey. It neither gives them a job nor marks them as logo-only. Next to the diazo ground (#1F4F8F), the logo blue is a second strong blue with no role, and the tile never shows how the two sit together.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds that must work inside this palette, and Mark, who is being asked whether his current colours carry over. As it stands, the tile gives no answer for the colours on his letterhead and logo file.

findings.where: Article specimen (An article page), the body text, pull quote and PDF link sitting on the gridded blueprint ground
findings.fault: Long-form reading text sits straight on the saturated diazo blue, and the grid lines run behind and through the lines of text. The brief treats the article page as a reading surface, yet it gets the same textured ground as the hero drawing, with no quieter ground for the text.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff reading one of Mark's full articles. Light text on strong blue, with lines crossing every row, is tiring over a whole essay. Angélique will also be adding long posts that all land on this ground.

findings.where: Nav bar title block: the ruled cells for Profile, Articles, Blog and Contact beside the Drawing MMM-GA-001 and Scale NTS cells (desktop row; phone top two rows)
findings.fault: Link cells and static label cells share one treatment: the same ruled box, the same light colour and no fill difference. Nothing on the surface tells the four links apart from the drawing number and scale, which do nothing.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning the bar for where to go. On a phone they may tap 'MMM-GA-001' expecting a page, and nothing happens.

findings.where: Hero drawing, the amber-hatched third arch, and the amber 'Write to Mark' button below it
findings.fault: Sodium amber has two jobs in the same view: lighting part of the drawing and marking the one action. The palette even labels it 'daylight in the drawing, and the one action'. So the button doesn't have its own colour, and the hatched arch looks just as 'live' as the button.
findings.who_objects: A visitor looking for what to do next. On the first screen the eye goes first to the amber arch, which does nothing, and only then to the button.
